tone_statements.citation: Kessié-Ouattara, Diane Laure & Yao Maxime Dido. 2025. Analyse morphosyntaxique des séries verbales en Nghlwa (Mbatto) [Morphosyntactic analysis of verbal series in Nghlwa (Mbatto)]. Akiri (Revue des sciences humaines et sociales, lettres, langues et civilisations) 3(4): 497-513.
tone_statements.quote: S’agissant du progressif, en l’occurrence, l’aspect se présente en un morphème bipartite ; la première s’adjoignant au sujet et la seconde, représentée par le ton haut, a pour support segmental chacun des verbes. [...] les deux verbes ayant en partage le ton bas, marqueur de l’accompli.
tone_statements.translation: As for the progressive, in this case, the aspect appears as a bipartite morpheme; the first part attaching to the subject and the second, represented by the high tone, having each of the verbs as its segmental support. [...] the two verbs sharing the low tone, marker of the perfective (accompli).
tone_statements.locator: pp. 502-503, section 5.1 (criteria for serial verb constructions, examples 4a-4b)

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en). 'Mbato language', revision of 6 Aug 2025 (phonology section sourced to Bôle-Richard 2018 and Bôle-Richard 1984)
sources.note: Tertiary. 'Mbato has a tonal system consisting of three level tones' (citing Bôle-Richard 2018); no nasal consonant phonemes; nothing at all on stress or accent.
Bibliographic only: confirms Thomas Blecke's talk 'Verb inflection in Nghlwa (/Mbato)'; no abstracts or papers are posted on the conference site.

sources.note: Only a general remark covering all 66 languages, p. 3: « Quant à l'accent tonique ou plutôt l'intonation, dont l'importance est souvent considérable dans les langues nègres.. il est impossible de donner ces indications au moyen de signes alphabétiques. » Nothing Mbato-specific; p. 11 ethnographic note says the Gwa language is very close to Kyama (Ebrié).

sources.citation: Kessié-Ouattara, Diane Laure & Yao Maxime Dido. 2025. Analyse morphosyntaxique des séries verbales en Nghlwa (Mbatto) [Morphosyntactic analysis of verbal series in Nghlwa (Mbatto)]. Akiri (Revue des sciences humaines et sociales, lettres, langues et civilisations) 3(4): 497-513.
sources.quote: S’agissant du progressif, en l’occurrence, l’aspect se présente en un morphème bipartite ; la première s’adjoignant au sujet et la seconde, représentée par le ton haut, a pour support segmental chacun des verbes. [...] les deux verbes ayant en partage le ton bas, marqueur de l’accompli.
sources.locator: pp. 502-503, section 5.1 (criteria for serial verb constructions, examples 4a-4b)
sources.note: Not a tone study, but first-hand and tone-marked throughout with three level-tone diacritics (acute, macron, grave, e.g. èē, ɓjḛ̄, bíɉà̰); states grammatical tone in the verb: the progressive is a bipartite morpheme whose second part is a HIGH tone realised on each verb of the series, and the accompli (perfective) is marked by a LOW tone shared by the verbs. No tone inventory section, nothing on stress/accent.

sources.note: Per the AfricaBib abstract: a tonological analysis of the non-verbal constituents of the Ngula dialect spoken at Domolon (speakers aged 15-25), with sections on the 'tonétique et tonématique des tons du ngula', a distributional and quantitative study of the tones, and a 'résolution du problème des mélodiques' (i.e. the status of contour/modulated tones); with tables. The number of tonemes is not given in the abstract (Wikipedia, after Bôle-Richard 2018, reports three level tones).
